children: Ford
raised the low end of its full-year profit outlook after another strong quarter, while setting a longer-term goal of reaching
8% adjusted EBIT margins by 2029
The automaker now expects
2026 adjusted EBIT of $10.5 billion to $11 billion

, up from its previous range of $10 billion to $11 billion. Adjusted free cash flow guidance remains at $6 billion to $7 billion, while capital expenditures are expected between $9.5 billion and $10.5 billion.
Ford generated
$49.5 billion in third-quarter revenue
, $2.7 billion in adjusted EBIT and $4.7 billion in adjusted free cash flow despite a short-term supplier disruption late in the quarter.
CEO Jim Farley said the company's strategy increasingly revolves around new vehicles, higher-margin software, services and parts, and a bigger push into
Ford Energy
That energy business is starting to show meaningful commercial traction.
Executed contracts and late-stage negotiations already cover more than
80% of Ford Energy's planned 2028 capacity
, while Ford remains on track to bring 20 gigawatt-hours of annual capacity online by the end of 2027.
Ford is also preparing a new generation of lower-cost vehicles.
Its upcoming international midsize pickup is expected to carry material costs about
20% below the current Ranger
, while the Louisville-built Fathom remains scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2027 with a starting MSRP of
. About 90% of validation testing has already been completed, although management said supply-base readiness remains the primary remaining risk.
Investor Takeaway
I think Ford's quarter is becoming less about simply defending its traditional truck business and more about whether management can build
higher-margin businesses around it
The raised 2026 guidance is encouraging, but management expects 2027 profitability to remain roughly flat as Ford absorbs around
$2 billion of headwinds from commodities, memory and logistics costs
, alongside F-150 downtime and continued investment in its electric-vehicle and energy platforms.
That makes the 2029 margin target important.
Ford needs software, parts, Ford Pro and Ford Energy to offset pressure from Model e, where the quarterly EBIT loss widened to
$1.1 billion
For investors, the key things to watch are
Ford Energy contracting, the Fathom launch, EV losses, F-150 inventory discipline and whether the company can hold profitability through 2027 before the next major earnings step-up arrives
Ford raised the near-term floor.
Now it has to prove it can lift the long-term margin ceiling.

title: Ford Gives Wall Street a Big Reason to Look Ahead
